reason: The cited evidence (all from the same paper) directly supports the key premises: E4 confirms full densification, grain refinement (~56% reduction), and high dislocation density at 15 GPa/1450 °C/10 min; E1 and E4 describe plastic deformation and dislocation multiplication as the densification mechanism; E1 states UHPS suppresses intragranular pores and grain growth; E4 links the microstructure to enhanced mechanical properties. The final premise linking reduced porosity to reduced hole formation in a plating bath is a logical extension but is not directly evidenced in the cited passages.
premises: UHPS at 15 GPa and 1450 °C for 10 min fully densifies ZrB2 with refined grains and high dislocation density
Plastic deformation and dislocation multiplication are the dominant densification mechanisms under UHPS
UHPS suppresses intragranular pores and grain growth compared to conventional high-temperature sintering
The refined, high-dislocation microstructure enhances mechanical properties
Reduced porosity from UHPS will directly reduce hole formation during liquid plating bath exposure
